Visa Establishes Global Capability Hubs in Singapore to Build the Future of Global Commerce
summary:
Visa, a global leader in digital payments, today announced the establishment of six global capability hubs at its new Solution Center in Singapore. Spanning AI, cybersecurity, quantum computing and next-generation payments, the hubs will develop technologies and solutions designed for deployment across Visa's global network.
For nearly five decades, Singapore has played a central role in Visa's mission to make commerce more trusted, secure and reliable across Asia Pacific. The new Solution Center at Paya Lebar Green deepens that commitment, bringing together more than 1,500 professionals across technology, product, cybersecurity, engineering and innovation. Visa also plans to further develop specialised research, engineering and innovation roles across areas such as AI, cybersecurity and quantum technologies.
"We're entering an extraordinary period of commerce innovation, driven by AI, digital money and other emerging technologies. Turning that promise into progress requires technology people and businesses can trust. Our expanded presence in Singapore will bring together great talent, deep expertise, and trusted infrastructure to build new commerce experiences around the world," said Rajat Taneja, President, Technology, Visa.
Building the capabilities for the next generation of commerce
The six capability hubs will focus on specialised areas where emerging technologies are creating new opportunities for how commerce moves, operates and stays secure. Together, they span three strategic domains:
Artificial Intelligence and Commerce:

Applied AI for payments and fintech use cases to responsibly advance the use of AI to improve commerce experiences, operational efficiency and decision-making.
Advances in agentic commerce to explore how AI agents can securely interact with merchants, consumers and payment networks.
Next-Generation Payments:

Research into the digital money, stablecoins and programmable payments ecosystem to support the evolution of money movement and new payment models
Wallets and alternate payment methods to help connect emerging payment experiences across multiple rails and networks.
Trust, Security and Resilience:

Cybersecurity to strengthen resilience and protection across increasingly complex digital ecosystems
Quantum computing for finance, researching applications of quantum technologies for financial services and preparing for a quantum-secure future.
"Singapore is increasingly where the future of commerce is being built. Many of the world's most complex questions around payments innovation, digital money, AI and trust are being solved in Asia Pacific. By bringing these capabilities together in Singapore, we are creating a hub that can develop globally relevant solutions while supporting Singapore's continued leadership in technology and innovation," said Stephen Karpin, Regional President, Asia Pacific, Visa.
Teams at Paya Lebar Green will collaborate with partners across academia, government, financial institutions and the fintech ecosystem to develop and scale next-generation technologies in Singapore, including AXS, DBS, DCS, FOMO Pay, Nium and StraitsX. Visa is also participating in the Monetary Authority of Singapore's BLOOM (Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency) initiative and engaging with academic and research institutions on emerging technologies, including quantum computing.
"Visa has been a long-standing partner with Singapore for over four decades. Visa's latest investment in six global capability hubs here will create new high-value jobs for Singaporeans. It will also bolster Singapore's role in developing innovative financial products and solutions in areas such as agentic commerce and quantum," said Beng Kong Pee, Executive Vice President, Singapore Economic Development Board.
By expanding its research, product development and engineering capabilities in Singapore, Visa aims to accelerate technologies that can be developed locally and deployed across its global network. To learn more about Visa's commitment to building trusted ways to pay, visit Visa at Singapore EXPO, Hall 2, Booth 2B25 at the Singapore FinTech Festival from 18-20 November 2026.

AlRayan Bank Selects Monument Technology as Strategic Partner for Landmark Technology Transformation
summary:
The UK’s longest-established Islamic bank is investing in technology to deliver capabilities that will rival many of the UK’s leading challenger banks.
AlRayan Bank, also the UK’s largest and most successful Islamic bank, has signed an agreement with Monument Technology to move onto a modern, cloud-based and modular banking platform.
Monument Technology’s award-winning ‘Bank in a Box’ Banking Platform as a Service (BPaaS) will provide the technology foundation for the Bank’s operations, bringing together best-of-breed capabilities across savings, current accounts, property finance products, customer servicing and digital channels within a single platform, with integration to regulatory and financial reporting.
The programme will help AlRayan Bank deliver enhanced digital services and more seamless customer experiences, while creating a simpler and more flexible technology environment and enabling new products to be launched more quickly.
Monument Technology took the original platform which is used by Monument Bank and is significantly developing it to serve the needs of other financial institutions, already including Ecology Building Society and Castle Trust Bank. Its modular design will give AlRayan Bank the flexibility to benefit from new capabilities and the upgrade or replacement of individual components as technology develops, without being forced to move to another technology provider.
It will be Monument’s first move into Islamic banking, as the sector continues to grow worldwide, with TheCityUK estimating that global Islamic finance assets will reach $10 trillion by 2030, and the UK accounting for 85% of Europe’s Islamic finance market.
Giles Cunningham, CEO of AlRayan Bank said: “This is the most significant technology investment AlRayan Bank has ever made. Start-up challengers have great technology and big banks have great brands. What we have is harder to copy: relationships with our customers built over more than twenty years, and values-based banking that they trust. This partnership will give us the technology to match.
“This agreement isn’t just a technology upgrade. It’s about giving customers the seamless digital banking they expect, and we hope it becomes a case study for how mid-sized, specialist banks can modernise without losing what makes them unique.”
Steve Britain, CEO of Monument Technology, said: “AlRayan Bank has a strong reputation, trusted relationships with its customers and ambitious plans for the future. Working with AlRayan Bank is an important step for Monument Technology, particularly as it takes us into Islamic banking and current accounts for the first time.
“Our approach is to give banks and building societies access to modern banking technology without the cost and complexity of developing and maintaining everything themselves. With three institutions now having selected our platform, we’re seeing growing interest in a model that allows banks to modernise while retaining control over how their businesses develop.”
The platform will be tailored to support the Bank’s Sharia-compliant product offering and operating model. The two organisations will now work together on detailed implementation planning, with the new platform introduced in phases to ensure customers can continue banking as normal while new capabilities and features are rolled out.

title: Encompass and Scottish Financial Enterprise Help KYC Professionals Build AI Agents at Agent Build Day
summary:
Encompass Corporation, the corporate digital identity (CDI) company behind the EC360 platform, has hosted an Agent Building Day in partnership with Scottish Financial Enterprise (SFE). The event brought together know your customer (KYC), operations and financial crime compliance professionals to build working AI agents for tasks they deal with in their day-to-day jobs.
Much of a KYC analyst’s day goes on work that adds little value: researching a company across registries and websites, re-keying the same details into more than one system, waiting days for an answer to a simple request, and judging which alerts and reviews deserve attention first. New starters face the steepest climb, because much of the know-how sits with experienced colleagues rather than in documented processes.
AI agents that can look up live company data are now practical. As AI changes how work gets done, everyone, from new joiners to experienced analysts, needs the chance to improve. The Agent Building Day was designed to deliver that, on the basis that the people who do KYC work every day are best placed to say where an agent would save time or improve a decision. No technical skills were required: if participants could describe a process, they could build an agent.
Participants from six organizations joined an opening icebreaker session where individuals interviewed each other about a slow, repetitive task they do often. Each team chose one problem and planned its agent on a build card. 
Ideas were grouped under two themes. Efficiency prompts focused on the same result in less time: replacing manual research with on-demand access to sources, removing re-keying and duplicate record-keeping, speeding up simple requests that sit in a queue for days, and chasing cases that have stalled. Efficacy prompts focused on a better result: applying risk ratings consistently, monitoring changes so analysts know where to focus, building complete company and ownership profiles from multiple checks, and giving new starters the guidance they would otherwise get from a senior colleague.
Teams built their agents, supported by Encompass facilitators and technical support. Each agent could request live company data and documents, such as registry records and ownership details, from EC360 through the EC360 model context protocol (MCP) connector, (an open standard for connecting AI agents to data sources). No client or bank data was used at any point.
Three prizes were awarded: Time Back, for the largest, realistic time saving; Better Call, for the agent that did most to improve the quality of a decision, or how well it can be justified to a reviewer or regulator; and Would Use It Monday, voted for by everyone in the room for the agent they would most want to use in their own job the following week. The day closed with demos, giving everyone the chance to see each build up close and talk to the other teams.
Participants left having built and presented a working agent, with practical experience of what agents can and cannot do. Organizations gained a set of agent ideas chosen by its own staff and tested in practice, each backed by a build card that states the problem, the expected time saving or quality improvement, and where a person stays in control.
Sandy Begbie CBE, CEO of Scottish Financial Enterprise said: “Scotland’s financial services sector has always thrived by combining world-class talent with a willingness to embrace change. The Encompass Agent Build Day turned that ambition into action. By bringing industry partners together to build, test and learn, we are helping our workforce develop the confidence and practical skills needed to lead the next chapter of financial services."
The event builds on Encompass’s Innovator series, including a program of AI-powered KYC roundtables in New York and London, which brought senior practitioners together to discuss the practical deployment of AI in KYC operations.
Terry Dawson, Chief Product and Technology Officer, Encompass Corporation, said: "The people closest to KYC and financial crime work are often the ones who see the best opportunities to improve it. The Agent Build Day gave them the chance to act on those ideas and build something real in a single afternoon. The energy in the room, and the quality of the agents the teams produced, showed how much talent and insight this generation brings. We're grateful to Scottish Financial Enterprise for partnering with us to make it happen."

PhotonPay Strengthens North American Regulatory Footprint With Canada's RPAA Registration
summary:
PhotonPay today announced that its Canadian operating entity, Photon Dance CA Inc., is now registered with the Bank of Canada as a payment service provider (PSP) under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). The entity was previously registered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as a Money Services Business (MSB). The RPAA registration further strengthens PhotonPay's regulatory foundation in Canada and supports its continued development of local financial services across North America.
The RPAA establishes a federal framework for the registration and supervision of PSPs conducting specified retail payment activities in Canada. Administered by the Bank of Canada, it sets requirements for operational risk management, incident response and regulatory reporting. PSPs that hold end-user funds are also required to implement measures to safeguard those funds, strengthening oversight and accountability across Canada's retail payments ecosystem.
The Canadian registration adds to PhotonPay's broader regulatory presence across North America. In the United States, PhotonPay is registered as a Money Services Business with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and holds money transmitter licenses across multiple U.S. states. Across the Americas, Europe and Asia, PhotonPay holds 35 payment licenses, regulatory authorizations and registrations, reflecting the regulatory breadth behind its operations across key financial markets.
For PhotonPay, building a global financial operating system requires more than connecting payment capabilities across markets. It also means developing the local regulatory and financial infrastructure needed to support those capabilities in each jurisdiction. As businesses expand internationally, their financial operations increasingly span different account structures, payment systems, currencies and regulatory environments. Bringing these functions together requires infrastructure that can address local market requirements while giving businesses a more unified way to manage their global finances.
This is the vision behind PhotonPay's next-generation Financial OS. Through an integrated, API-first architecture, PhotonPay brings together multi-asset wallets, local collections, global payouts, foreign exchange, card issuing and embedded finance. By supporting both fiat currencies and stablecoins within its broader financial infrastructure, the platform connects traditional payment rails with emerging digital-asset capabilities, helping businesses manage increasingly complex financial operations across markets.
"Global financial infrastructure must be designed around the realities of the markets it serves. Regulatory frameworks, payment systems and the responsibilities involved in handling funds differ across jurisdictions, and these differences need to be accounted for at the infrastructure level," said JP Pi, Global Chief Compliance Officer at PhotonPay. "Our approach is to build a Financial OS that brings together global capabilities while respecting the regulatory and operational requirements of each local market. The RPAA registration is another step in putting that approach into practice, as we continue developing infrastructure to support businesses operating across an increasingly interconnected financial landscape."

FiX27: One Caribbean Founder Is Heading to Silicon Valley for a Shot at US$1 Million
summary:
Barbados is set to host the Startup World Cup Caribbean Regional  Semi-Final on January 29, 2027, during the fourth annual FiX27 powered by Fintech Islands,  which runs January 27–29, 2027, at Wyndham Grand Resort Sam Lord’s Castle. The winner of  the Caribbean Regional Semi-Final will advance to the Startup World Cup Global Finale in Silicon  Valley, with a shot at US$1 million in investment. 
This addition to the FiX conference will bring the region’s most promising entrepreneurs face-to face with top international investors. The announcement marks a significant milestone for Fintech  Islands, reflecting its continued mission of fostering financial innovation, entrepreneurship and  investment in the Caribbean. 
A Global Platform for Caribbean Innovation 
Applications are now open to select the ten leading Caribbean startups, who will pitch before more  than 30 international investors managing a collective US$10 billion in capital on January 29, 2027. Applications close January 1, 2027, and are open to early-stage fintech startups, from pre-seed to  Series A, with a working product or pilot. The winning founder will advance to the Global Finale,  which attracts an audience of more than 2,500 investors and 50,000 attendees. Founders can apply  at www.startupworldcup.io/barbados-2026 
The competition offers Caribbean entrepreneurs the opportunity to gain international visibility and  compete alongside startups from around the world. 
Allison Hunte, Co-Founder and CEO of Fintech Islands, said, “Hosting the regional competition  is an opportunity for us to help close the gap between Caribbean innovation and global investment,  giving founders greater access to the networks, expertise and capital that can support business  growth beyond their local markets.”
She added that by connecting Caribbean innovators with top international and regional investors,  the event aims to accelerate the growth of the regional fintech landscape and drive financial  inclusion across the islands. 
Beyond the Startup World Cup: What to Expect at FiX27 
FiX27 brings more than 100 speakers from 15 countries to Barbados, including investors, bankers,  regulators and business leaders, for over 25 hours of sessions, and is expected to welcome more  than 600 attendees. The programme covers the issues that reach a business owner’s bottom line: 
• Getting paid: faster, cheaper ways to accept payments from customers at home, across the  region and overseas, and why sending money between Caribbean islands still costs more  than it should. 
• The rules: how regulators are updating financial rules for digital payments, and what that  means for businesses that use them. 
• Digital money: what stablecoins and central bank digital currencies are, and whether they  matter to a small business. 
• Using your financial data: how open finance lets businesses share their banking records  securely to access credit and better services. 
• Funding growth: how investors and lenders decide who gets capital, and how Caribbean  businesses can put themselves in that position. 
Hunte said this year’s conference is open to any business that moves money in the region. “Across  four editions, FiX has brought fintech founders, banks and regulators into the same room. This  year, we’re opening that room to every Caribbean business. If you take payments from overseas  customers or pay suppliers on another island, the decisions discussed at FiX27 affect your costs,  and you should be part of that conversation.” 
True to its Caribbean roots, the FiX27 experience extends beyond the conference sessions,  combining business and cultural experiences that showcase the region’s hospitality, food and  music with opportunities for networking, knowledge-sharing and deal-making. 
For more information on Fintech Islands, visit https://www.fintechislands.com/ For more information on the Startup World Cup Caribbean Regional Semi-Final, visit: https://www.startupworldcup.io/barbados-2026
